resume_rules.explanation: All stages skip completed and verified cases. Trace skips any case where the record and all 48 NPZs verify. Channel workers claim eligible units via non-blocking flock and skip verified shards and sidecars. If a process was killed uncleanly, remove stale RUNNING markers before restarting. Stale FAILED case files require --retry-failed to re-attempt (otherwise skipped).
resume_rules.flock_behavior: Claims and job locks use OS fcntl.flock and are automatically released on process exit/termination.

stop_rule.natural_threshold: 3 or more failures out of 120 cases per map stops the map (2 allowed)
stop_rule.challenge_threshold: 1 or more failures out of 23 cases per map stops the map (0 allowed)

lead_relaunch_20261110.root_cause: Each PyNEC xq_card on a resident context leaks a result set (~0.116 MB/solve). Workers grew to the 24 GiB ulimit -v (C++ bad_alloc, shown by SWIG as 'Unknown exception' - this is the Rotterdam error), then host RAM ran out (numpy 'Unable to allocate'), then the OOM killer hit w2. Traces were complete; no physics or data failure.
lead_relaunch_20261110.fix: scripts/build_bench_production_channels.py: each unit runs in a forked child (leak dies with it); MemoryError / 'Unknown exception' / SIGKILLed child are transient (3 attempts, backoff 300 s then 900 s, never FAILED until exhausted); real exception type and traceback recorded; 4 GiB free-RAM admission check. Tests: tests/test_bench_production_channels_isolation.py
